I do not believe this is a duplicate of the cited reports, and I would prefer to keep it open for investigation.

The distinguishing observation is that my weekly meter reconciles exactly with the same visible spend, while the monthly meter does not:

- Subscription age: less than 24 hours
- Actual/visible spend: $5.70
- Weekly: 19% of $30 = $5.70 — exact match
- Monthly: 40% of $60 = $24.00 — does not match

So this is not a case where all quota windows disagree with usage history. It is a first-day, window-specific inconsistency: the weekly calculation is internally consistent, while the monthly calculation is approximately 4.2× higher.

#42549 concerns the 5-hour rolling window, which is not the behavior reported here. #41206 and #41976 may be related, but neither presents this exact weekly-correct/monthly-incorrect first-day comparison.

Please investigate whether the monthly Go-plan meter is using a different accounting source, billing-cycle boundary, or display calculation than the weekly meter, and confirm whether the displayed 40% represents actual quota consumption. I need an accurate reading of the $60 monthly cap to plan usage without unexpected loss of inference access.

### Models

This `_ide` suffix issue happens **only on Claude models** (Anthropic-compatible provider, `npm: @ai-sdk/anthropic`, `baseURL` pointing at a local 9router).

Confirmed:

- claude-sonnet-5
- claude-opus-5
- claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
- claude-fable-5
- ag-claude-sonnet-4-6
- ag-claude-opus-4-6-thinking

Non-Claude models on the same provider (Grok, Gemini, DeepSeek) did not show this.

The `_ide` suffix is applied after the advertised tool name. Remap proxy log (`20127`) rewrites `bash_ide` / `read_ide` / `write_ide` on the Claude path.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #34878: Similar symptom (backspace broken, ctrl+h works as workaround) but attributed to a different encoding root cause (ConPTY sending `0x08` vs `0x7F`). The fix there may already address or relate to KKP `\x1b[127u` handling.

For keybind-related issues, please also check our pinned keybinds documentation: #4997

Run into this with TinyFish MCP (https://agent.tinyfish.ai/mcp, Clerk OAuth, single-use rotating refresh tokens) on opencode 0.0.0-next-17236.

After the access token expires, every session start reports needs_auth and forces manual re-auth. I verified the persisted refresh token is still valid. The token endpoint returns HTTP 200 with fresh tokens, yet opencode won't use it. Post-refresh, Clerk invalidates the old refresh token via `invalid_grant`, so any stale attempt leaves the creds permanently broken until a full re-auth. A single successful refresh consumes the rotation before opencode can persist it, which matches #34074/#34523.
